jokes.text: Once the egg descends into the fallopian tube-- / Oh, wait, oh, get out of here!
jokes.setup: Monica is trying to explain to Chandler why they need to leave quickly for another ovulation attempt.
jokes.punchline: Ross interrupts with 'Get out of here!' — horrified by his sister discussing her egg descending into her fallopian tube at the dinner table, in front of him.
jokes.explanation: Ross's horror at his sister's clinical description of her reproductive process is a solid sibling cringe beat. The specificity of 'fallopian tube' is what triggers his revulsion. Standard but effective.

jokes.text: I sincerely hope the rest of your party is returning. / No, just me. All alone. / Dinner for six for one. Well, you boys are about to see something really special.
jokes.setup: Everyone has left. Joey is alone at the birthday dinner table with all the food.
jokes.punchline: Joey's 'you boys are about to see something really special' — addressed to the waitstaff — framing his solo assault on six people's food as a performance worth witnessing.
jokes.explanation: A perfect Joey ending. 'You boys are about to see something really special' — delivered with complete sincerity and pride — is an extraordinary line. Joey treats eating as a performance art worthy of an audience. The image of him alone at a table for six with all the food is a great visual. The confidence and self-awareness coexist in a way that's uniquely Joey. Among the top 3 moments of the episode.

jokes.text: How was everything? / Excellent. The shrew, in particular, was exquisite.
jokes.setup: The waiter checks in after the meal.
jokes.punchline: Chandler reports that 'the shrew, in particular, was exquisite' — completing the joke that the manipulative shrew was a real dish that was consumed.
jokes.explanation: A beautiful callback landing. Chandler completes the manipulative shrew bit by treating it as an actual dish he consumed and reviewing it. 'Exquisite' as a review of his wife is simultaneously a compliment and a continuation of the insult. The triple callback (shrew joke + Monica's behavior + restaurant plot) is elegant. Very quotable.

jokes.text: Joey. Joey. [waiter trying to wake a passed-out/sleeping Joey]
jokes.setup: Joey boasted he was about to show the waiters 'something really special' by eating all the food.
jokes.punchline: The waiter is now trying to rouse Joey — presumably passed out or catatonic from eating six people's worth of food.
jokes.explanation: A perfect visual button to the episode. Joey promised something special; what he delivered was apparently eating himself into unconsciousness. The waiter just calling 'Joey. Joey.' — presumably while Joey is unresponsive — is a great image that requires no words. The payoff to the food-eating subplot is exactly right.

jokes.text: This is the best birthday ever!
jokes.setup: Phoebe is not at the restaurant — she's left for Mike. Meanwhile the birthday dinner has been a total disaster.
jokes.punchline: Phoebe calls in declaring 'This is the best birthday ever!' — she's deliriously happy because she's with Mike, completely oblivious to or indifferent to the chaos she left behind.
jokes.explanation: A perfect ironic final button. Phoebe declaring the worst birthday dinner in history 'the best birthday ever' because she's with her boyfriend is both completely in character and structurally satisfying. The irony is total — the audience knows exactly how terrible the dinner was. Great closing joke.

jokes.text: Joey. Joey. — [Joey still eating, oblivious] — This is the best birthday ever!
jokes.setup: Phoebe has returned (presumably with Mike). Joey is still eating from the enormous order he placed.
jokes.punchline: Joey is too deep in food to respond to anyone; Phoebe, having escaped for her boyfriend and returning to find Joey in a food coma, declares it 'the best birthday ever' — the irony being that the evening was objectively terrible.
jokes.explanation: Good visual closer. Joey still eating is a physical payoff to his food obsession throughout the episode. Phoebe's declaration of 'best birthday ever' despite everything that went wrong is a sweet, funny, slightly absurdist button that ends the episode on the right note.

tmdb_overview: The friends are looking forward to getting together and celebrating Phoebe's birthday. However, on the day of the party, Ross struggles to convince Rachel to leave Emma with Mrs. Geller babysitting, and Monica and Chandler get into an argument, after Monica discovers that he's been smoking. All of this causes them to be incredibly late, leaving Phoebe and Joey alone at a restaurant with a table for six.
insight: Phoebe's birthday dinner lands 70 jokes but struggles to land them meaningfully.
